version.value: 1942 work for narrator and orchestra; narration in English
version.note: The LP calls it A Lincoln Portrait. This is the orchestral work, not Walter Beeler’s band transcription. The performing edition and session alterations are unknown.

performers.note: All three are explicitly credited on Columbia MS 6040. No individual orchestral players are identified.

date.note: 1959 is the documented carrier issue year; a session date has not been established from the consulted carrier evidence.

place.note: The orchestra’s name does not establish a particular studio or concert venue.

label.note: US stereo vinyl LP; sleeve explicitly identifies the stereo release.

catalogue.note: Archive catalogue dates this carrier to 1959; the sleeve also carries Library of Congress catalogue numbers beginning R59.

matrixTakeSides.note: The selected segmented file contains the complete Lincoln Portrait. Matrix, take and stamper identifiers are unknown.

credits.note: Institutional transfer credit; no independently established personal mastering credit.

composition.value: Copyrighted Copland composition; musical-work permissions administered by Boosey & Hawkes
composition.note: Lincoln’s nineteenth-century speeches and Copland’s twentieth-century musical work are distinct rights objects. No permission for republication of the complete composition or a modern score is asserted.

recording.value: Territorial EU phonogram public-domain basis: commercial publication in 1959, before 1963
recording.note: Under the project’s eu-published-before-1963 rule, the documented commercial carrier’s former 50-year phonogram term had expired before the 2013 extension. This includes the recorded narration as part of the phonogram assessment. It is not US or worldwide clearance, not a Creative Commons licence and not a US-government recording; composition rights remain separate.

rights.creditLine: Aaron Copland, Lincoln Portrait; Carl Sandburg, narrator; New York Philharmonic, André Kostelanetz. Columbia Masterworks MS 6040 (1959 issue), Internet Archive LP transfer. Territorial EU phonogram basis only; Copland composition remains copyrighted.
